page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Notes in the right margin, beside the text lines. Page number top right. Running head top centre. Catchword and gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: In laminis quoq; ferreis aut aneis &c. ci-ffime[?] panes coquuntur, Vnde lixa in militia ta-les laminas vt & farinam, in facculis coriaceis, nefcilicet peruolet, fecum gerunt, vt fugati vel exutinere defatigati, cibum in eiusmodi lami-nis cito poffint parare. Sed & furnos fubter-raneos ad colles (fcil. & montes, vbi glebofum fo-lum eft, quidam fodiunt, quod hodie Turcas factitare audio: alii vero fornaces cupreas pen-files fecum vehunt currum in flar fufpenfi-lum.

Damnantur autem omnes qui feruenti loco, cineribus atq; carbone torrentur, intus au-tem crudi existunt. Qui pa-nes da-mnētur ob coctu-ram ratio-nem?Subcineritius vero coctura ratione omnium improbatur maxime, barbaris & a cultu humanitatis remotis conuenientes: minus ab igne vsti, æqueq, intus & extra coctu in-nocentiores deprehenduntur, vt sunt panes fornis coctu. Non hic praetereundum est, ab vrbe condita annis super quingentis ostogin-ta Pistores Romae non fuisse mulierum, id tunc opus fuisse, ipsos, Quirites panes finxisse. Vxor Catonis, autore Plutarcho, pinsendi munus à sua dignitate alienum non putauit: Denique vero Persia atq; Asia omnis generis delitiæ Romanorum confluxerunt, unde adhuc pistores illi dulciarii, qui placentas & catera dulcia panificia format, carnes incrustant, vt in amplis vrbibus, magnatum familiis videre est.Pistores ab vrbe condita annis 580. Romæ fuerunt nulli.

page.notes: Printed text is dense and some words are uncertain: "ci-ffime" (marked [?]), the run of "Sed & furnos" and "fubter-raneos", the bracketed words "(fcil." and "fo-lum", and the Greek-period-looking marks in "Vnde" line were read with reasonable confidence but should be checked against the scan. The running head "PRoRO GANDA A." is uncertain; it may be a longer title partly hidden by the page edge. Right-margin notes were transcribed as printed, with the note hyphenation kept. Signature "Oi" and catchword "De" are read from the foot of the page; the signature may be "O 2" or similar. The page number "211" is printed as "2II" in the scan.
